coverage_gaps: The available routes do not include a dedicated preprint server, citation-graph provider, DOI metadata service, patent database, or non-FDA regulator; preprints, formal forward-citation traversal, patent status, and non-US regulatory conclusions therefore require separate documented follow-up.
PubMed indexing and publication-date fields can lag online-first release or corrections; cutoff eligibility requires manual date reconciliation for potentially decisive records.
ClinicalTrials.gov may omit non-US or unregistered early mechanistic studies, and registry records may not expose complete results or all publication links.
FDA searches may establish US regulatory status and dated safety evidence but cannot establish absence of worldwide development, approval, or regulator concern.
Non-English full texts and inaccessible historical pedigree reports may require translation or document retrieval before their evidentiary contribution can be judged.
exclusion_criteria: Record was first publicly available after 2024-12-31 and supplies no eligible earlier version.
LRRK2 or Parkinson disease appears only as incidental background without genetic, biochemical, physiological, biomarker, safety, or translational evidence relevant to the question.
A claimed substrate is supported solely by an unvalidated high-throughput hit with no direct phosphorylation or independent functional follow-up.
The study uses an uninterpretable mixture, undefined reagent, or assay lacking a usable LRRK2-specific comparison and cannot support any scoped claim.
Editorials, news items, conference listings without sufficient methods or results, and unsourced narrative claims are excluded from evidentiary synthesis but may trigger anchor searches.
Patents and chemistry-only records are excluded from biological-mechanism conclusions unless an independently verifiable peer-reviewed, trial, or regulatory record supplies the relevant evidence.
Duplicate database entries are excluded as separate evidence units after their query-to-record links and version relationships have been preserved.

Non-Parkinson neurodegenerative or inflammatory studies are excluded when they provide no transferable evidence about LRRK2 enzymology, physiological substrates, pathway function, safety, or target engagement.
inclusion_criteria: Record is available on or before 2024-12-31 after reconciling online-first, issue, correction, registry-update, regulatory effective, and database dates.

Primary human genetic evidence reports linkage, segregation, variant association, ancestry-specific frequency or effect, penetrance, phenotype, or functional interpretation relevant to LRRK2 and Parkinson disease.

Mechanistic evidence directly measures LRRK2 kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, conformation, localization, interaction, substrate phosphorylation, or a downstream cellular consequence in a defined experimental system.

Physiological-substrate claims include direct phosphorylation or site evidence plus endogenous expression, perturbation, inhibitor sensitivity, genetic dependency, patient-material support, or orthogonal validation sufficient to distinguish a substrate from an in vitro candidate.
Human carrier, sporadic-disease, postmortem, patient-derived cell, biofluid, or target-engagement studies are eligible when they test the mechanism or its generality.
Animal, cellular, and cell-free studies are eligible when organism, construct, expression context, variant, dose, and assay permit appraisal of relevance and overexpression or model artifacts.
Systematic reviews and focused reviews are eligible for terminology and citation expansion, while mechanistic conclusions are traced to and supported by primary records.
Registered trials and FDA regulatory records are eligible when they address LRRK2-targeted intervention, target engagement, biomarker performance, safety, approval status, or translational failure.

Null, negative, conflicting, failed-replication, correction, retraction, incomplete-penetrance, population-limited, and safety findings are eligible regardless of whether they support the leading mechanism.

For duplicate reports, preserve every query-to-record occurrence, merge only canonical records using PMID, DOI, NCT, regulatory identifier, and bibliographic checks, and retain distinct cohorts, follow-ups, corrections, and registry versions.

question_frame: Target-mechanism frame: in Parkinson disease and relevant human cellular, animal, and biochemical systems, determine how LRRK2 genetic discoveries and disease-associated variants support a causal relationship; how kinase, ROC-COR GTPase, and related cellular activities alter physiological substrates and pathways; and which penetrance, population, model, replication, null, or contradictory findings limit the mechanism's strength or generality. Search scope is database inception through 2024-12-31, with emphasis on primary genetic linkage/association, segregation and penetrance studies, biochemical and structural studies, endogenous-substrate validation, patient-derived material, perturbation studies, systematic reviews used for citation expansion, registered trials, and FDA regulatory records. Include humans and mechanistically informative mammalian, cellular, and cell-free systems; retain all languages when an English title or abstract permits screening, and escalate potentially decisive non-English records for translation. Separate genetic causality, enzymatic mechanism, physiological-substrate, disease-model, biomarker, and translational-intervention branches; preserve publication, online-first, correction, retraction, registry-update, jurisdiction, and effective dates so the as_of cutoff can be replayed.
stop_rules: Complete all planned sentinel, discovery, confirmation, expansion, challenge, and update queries across every route in source_map, recording exact query, execution timestamp, cutoff handling, result count, and provider version.
Do not begin broad screening until the 2004 genetic-discovery anchors and Rab-substrate anchors are recovered or their absence has triggered alias and query-field expansion.
Escalate unresolved conflicts in variant nomenclature, cohort overlap, phosphorylation-site assignment, registry-publication linkage, correction status, or cutoff date before synthesis.

Run backward and forward citation or author expansion from each decisive genetic-discovery, enzymatic-mechanism, and physiological-substrate anchor; stop expansion after two consecutive completed waves add no decision-relevant eligible evidence.

Require at least one dedicated challenge pass covering penetrance, ancestry, sporadic disease, negative or discordant mechanism results, model limitations, toxicity, corrections, and retractions before declaring saturation.

Stop a branch when its planned sources are complete, anchor checks pass, duplicates and versions are reconciled, and further retrieval is unlikely to change the branch conclusion or confidence rating.
If the retrieval budget is reached before saturation, stop deterministically, identify the unfinished branch and last completed query, and report the branch as non-exhaustive.
Treat changes in result counts as database-version observations; rerun the stored exact query for updates without silently replacing prior results or query-to-record links.
